key_results: The Dindshenchas, poems of Irish place-names transcribed in the 12th century, record the tale.
Coincheann killed Áed Minbhrec, son of the god Dagda, who had seduced his wife.
He carried the body on his back until he found a stone of equal size and set it down at the hillfort of Grianán Aileach.

text: Corrgenn, the hero also styled Coincheann, belongs to Irish legend. The Dindshenchas, verse devoted to Irish place-names and set down in the twelfth century, records that Coincheann slew Áed Minbhrec. That man, a son of the god Dagda, had lured Coincheann's own wife away. Coincheann was made to heft the victim himself, trudging on until he came to stones whose weight matched the body, and there he buried it. He finally set the burden down at Grianán Aileach, a celebrated hillfort.
